Barricades, vertical panels, drums, cones and tubes are the channeling devices that alert drivers to work zone hazards and guide them safely through, and at night they often carry flashing or steady-burn lights.
Large flashing or sequencing arrow panels may be used in work zones day and night to guide drivers into certain lanes and to tell them that part of the road ahead is closed.

The diagonal stripes on a barricade or vertical panel point toward the side traffic should pass, so stripes sloping downward to the right mean bear right and stripes sloping downward to the left mean bear left.
Flaggers wearing orange vests, shirts or jackets use red-orange flags or stop and slow paddles to stop, slow or guide traffic safely through work zones.
Barricade stripes sloping downward to the right tell the driver to bear right, and stripes sloping downward to the left tell the driver to bear left.
